about: Inviting and the army: the 💌s, the leash and its chains, the bond, berries, follower buffs.

berries.what: Berries on the bushes of every area, which her creatures eat to evolve.

decisions.quote: tie the cost to strength
Double the amount of berries animals need to evolve
decisions.rest: cost.per halved from 7.25
the level gap of made the youth's 6, 8 and 16 for light, normal and strong species

decisions.quote: We can change 6/8/16=>3/4/8, and reduce berry spawns (keep the current cluster size but reduce frequency of clusters.)
decisions.rest: a youth showing a dot per berry eaten, two rows of 4 at most:: cost.per back to 7.25, so 3, 4 and 8, and bushesPerArea and perArea halved, half as many patches of the same size, the same share of their bushes in berry

decisions.quote: we can make the berry clusters bigger

decisions.rest: legends are the areas' own, never grown

decisions.quote: No animal eats on its own
decisions.rest: only the bottom of her stack eats, fed by her with the sigil button; the detour knob (Ed, v233) and the baby's reach at its placed sigil (2026-10-11) gone with it

decisions.quote: There should be twice the number of patches as there are now.
decisions.rest: bushesPerArea 10 → 20 (patches the same size, so twice as many) and perArea [5, 8] → [10, 16], the same share of their bushes in berry as on 2026-10-27; an eaten berry still regrows at once elsewhere (Ed: "That's intended; you exhaust an area and then need to explore to find more.")

berries.notes: Berries and evolving (Ed): every area (not home's dancefloor clearing) has bushesPerArea berry bushes (normal bushes of that area) and perArea [min, max] berries on distinct ones at the start, both for an area 112 m across and grown with the area's ground (rules/berries.ts berryCounts: at today's 196 m areas, × 3.06, 61 bushes and 32–49 berries an area, measured on the fox and bear islands). Bushes grow in patches of patch.bushes [min, max] within patch.radius metres, spread evenly over the area at least patch.spacing apart, and none within a stump's fighting arena (stumpClear; Ed, 2026-11-06). No animal eats on its own (Ed, 2026-11-03; see feed): the bottom of her stack eats a berry she feeds it, walking over and eating it (eatTime seconds). The berry grows again at once on a free berry bush somewhere else on the map. A party animal evolves on the next bar line once it has eaten the berries its next level costs [1]: the fighting value it gains (cost.by "value": √(hp × dps), its species' strength included) at cost.per a berry, rounded, at least 1: so a berry buys the same fighting value for every species; one of normal strength costs 4 and 4 [2][3][4] ("power" would count hp × dps instead). Bigger patches since [5]: perArea and patch.bushes up a quarter to a half, so the first evolve's extra berry (2, was 1) and weaker species' one-berry minimum come out a little faster to feed than before. Evolving stops at adult [6].

berries.patch.spacing.what: The least distance between two berry patches' centres, in metres: patches spread evenly over each area, never nearer each other than this.

decisions.quote: I think we should change this process to more evenly distribute patches in the area, and also increase the clearance from the stump (not the middle).
decisions.rest: patch centres were a random angle and distance (0.15 to 0.65 of the area) from the area's middle, so they bunched; now each is the best of 24 random spots on the area's bush ground, the one farthest from every patch already placed, its own area's and its neighbours' (best-candidate blue noise), and at least spacing from all of them

berries.patch.spacing.notes: A floor, not the usual gap: the sampler spaces patches as far apart as the ground allows (about 50 m apart on average at 196 m areas, measured on the fox and bear islands), and spacing only binds in a cramped area, where an area that has no room left for another patch at this spacing stops short of its bushes. 16 m (about 4.5 patch radii) fits every area of the fox island and all but one of the bear island's at today's doubled count (Ed, 2026-11-06), with no area below 87% of its bushes; 18 m left two short, 20 m three. Each patch's centre keeps its whole patch inside its own area (patch.radius off the rim); the old 0.65 cap from the middle is gone, as patches now spread over the whole area.

berries.stumpClear.what: Metres past every stump's fighting arena that berry bushes and mushrooms also keep out of: 0 keeps them just outside the arena, 55 m from the stump today.

decisions.quote: I think we should change this process to more evenly distribute patches in the area, and also increase the clearance from the stump (not the middle).
decisions.rest: measured from the stump (rules/map.ts soundsystemSpot), which since the 50 m site gaps stands off the area's middle; before, the only clearance was the stump's 17 m roots clearing (runeMarkers.stump.clear), and patch centres kept 0.15 of the area from its middle, not the stump
berries outside the stump's fight zone: the clearance is the stump's arena's whole extent, arena.radius + arena.band (55 m, both times fight.scale), plus this knob, so it follows the arena

decisions.quote: Mushrooms shouldn't grow on berry patches, paths, stump fight areas, etc.
decisions.rest: the mushrooms keep the same clearance from every stump (rules/mushrooms.ts)

berries.stumpClear.notes: rules/map.ts stumpClearance: (arena.radius + arena.band) × fight.scale + stumpClear, never below 0, from the nearest stump (rules/map.ts stoneGap: its own area's or a neighbour's). The arena (rules/map.ts arenaOpen) is open round both the area's middle and its stump; only the stump's counts here. A berry patch's centre keeps stumpClearance + patch.radius, so no bush grows nearer. An area with too little ground beyond it keeps fewer bushes rather than grow them in the arena: measured at 55 m with spacing 16, every fox area has all 61 bushes, and one of the bear island's 30 areas has 53 of 61 (87%). Below 0 lets bushes and mushrooms into the arena's outer band (e.g. −10: 45 m).

berries.colour.what: The berries' colour: a deep berry pink.

decisions.quote: Berries: deep berry pink, instead of red.
decisions.rest: red is the warnings' colour; a shiny dark cherry red (#9e1024) before, which colourGrammar old brings back

berries.glow.what: How strongly a berry's soft halo glows.
berries.glow.notes: its soft halo's strength. B (debug) feeds the nearest party animal one berry. babyCost berries evolve a baby into a youth (one: Ed, 2026-10-11).

berries.feed.what: Feeding on command: a tap of the sigil button feeds the bottom of her stack a berry within reach of her; holding it puts that sigil down instead.

decisions.quote: something she does deliberately and accurately under time pressure
decisions.rest: no animal eats on its own; only the bottom of her stack, the one cycle moves through; each press queues one more berry, no hold-to-repeat

decisions.quote: otherwise feeding berries becomes a way of moving creatures quickly rather than levelling them up
decisions.rest: speed: it goes to its berry at about its own pace, 1 to 1.2 times

decisions.quote: just "[E]" (or equivalent controller) key above the berry with a little down arrow, and the berry glows brighter
decisions.rest: the prompt's words gone; glow, how much brighter the offered berry glows

berries.feed.notes: reach: metres from her a berry may be to be fed (the nearest un-taken one, glowing brighter, the key over it). speed: the animal walks to each queued berry at its leash pace times this. hold: seconds the sigil button is held, with a feed on offer, to put the bottom sigil down instead of feeding it (a tap shorter than this feeds). glow: how many times brighter the berry a tap would feed glows (its halo bigger and brighter, its core lit up; 1 the pulsing halo it had), the use key over it with a small down arrow and no words [3].

invites.what: The 💌 invite: on the ground she fires spinning love letters at creatures to win them over.

decisions.rest: issue #87

decisions.quote: base invite should be one envelope at a time (rebalance hits accordingly), they should arc a little and disappear when they hit the ground, go 50% further, 20% faster, and they should rotate by pitching instead of yawing

decisions.rest: balance, the overnight pass, with the wider level gap

decisions.quote: it feels like animals move faster than invitations so it's hard to land a hit. And ranges feel small
decisions.rest: speed 45 (was 31.2), range 42 (was 33), homingRange 14 (was 10); homing and homingCone unchanged; the animals' waiting distance held where it was (combatWaiting.inviteReach 33), and ?invites=old flies the old letters to A/B

invites.notes: The 💌 invite [1], replacing the proximity chat when on: on the ground she shoots spinning 💌s, aimed with the cursor (click fires) or the right stick (a trigger fires), or 1 toward the cursor. A burst is burst volleys burstGap seconds apart, each multiShot letters fanned over spread degrees, then cooldown seconds before the next; letters fly at speed m/s for range metres, turning toward the nearest invitable creature within homingRange metres and homingCone degrees of straight ahead at up to homing degrees a second, and land on one whose body comes within radius metres. Each hit adds amount to its affection; Round 11 [2]: one 💌 a shot (burst 1, multiShot 1), cooldown 0.55 (just over the old 0.5 s per-creature gap), hits [4, 9, 18, 36] so a meter fills in about the time it did with bursts of three (they gave one hit each 0.84 s); then [3] [4, 7, 14, 36]: the young and adults quicker to win over, so good play counts for more (a skilled player lasts about 2.5 minutes longer, a crude one no longer), range 33 (was 22) and speed 31.2 (was 26). Then [4]: speed 45 (was 31.2: faster than the witch on the ground, 19.25, and well clear of animals running in a fight, about 14), range 42 (was 33), homingRange 14 (was 10); a letter takes 0.93 s to its full range (was 1.06 s). The animals' waiting room no longer follows this range (combatWaiting.inviteReach), so the longer letters reach the circling animals; ?invites=old flies 31.2 / 33 / 10 to A/B.

invites.arc.what: the height (m) its lob rises over the straight line from her hand to the ground at its range, where it lands, with a puff (drawn only: the rules fly it flat).

invites.hits.what: How many letters it takes to win a creature over by its level, and how fast its meter drains when not being hit.

decisions.quote: the invitation dropoff rate (the speed at which animals become less invited) is too fast
decisions.rest: 0.03 after 4 s, a full meter in about 33 s; it was states.json's 0.08 after 1.5 s, this knob unread

decisions.quote: I think we should remove the 0.5s cooldown between counted hits per creature - better to control this through the witch firing speed instead of having hits not register
let's change the drain rate to 2% instead of 3%
decisions.rest: 0.02 after 4 s, a full meter in about 50 s; hearts from her animals' blows fade the same, in one queue with the 💌s ("this should be the same speed as 💌s fade ... and they go in the same fade 'queue'")

invites.hits.notes: letters to fill it, by level (baby, young, adult, legend; no baby is invitable since Ed, 2026-10-31); it drains drain of a full meter a second when not being hit, from config/states.json's affection.drainDelay seconds after the last [1]. Every letter that lands on an invitable creature counts [2]: how fast she invites is her firing rate (burst, burstGap, cooldown), nothing adaptive. Enraged creatures and legends block letters; scenery never stops them (Ed).

invites.wonAway.what: a creature she has won over whose sigil waits in its stone's stack roams its area with its happy roam and keeps `radius` m from any creature fighting her or with her, out of her fights' way.

quote: they should roam the whole area, and avoid creatures that are fighting. Do this in a simple way - we just want them out of the way of the fight
Newly won creatures can't be grabbed until the spell is cast, so they don't need to be near
decisions.rest: on #1804, through the coordinator: first for the challenge circle's won ones, then every area's; happy ones defending their area against enraged attackers in a wave keep doing that; one shared helper with its own switch and radius slider, on by default.

invites.wonAway.notes: The fighters are wild ones hunting a witch (rules/hunt.ts) and her followers with a fight's target; enraged besiegers aren't, so happy defenders aren't pushed off their defence, and one itself in a fight is moved by combat as ever. One within `radius` of a fighter walks straight away from the nearest at 1.5 times its pace; a roam target that near is drawn again in its area by its own seeded draws. Their sigils stay in the stack wherever they roam, so the spell (or the wave) scatters them round the stone as ever. Off: they roam as before, fights or no. rules/wonKeepAway.ts.

invites.fireSlow.what: her ground speed while firing, times this.

invites.inaccuracy.what: degrees either side of her aim each 💌 may go (a fixed hash of its number, so the same throws go the same ways); 0, dead straight, and a bag adds its own (config/wardrobe.json invitesAdd).

decisions.quote: For things with rapid rate of fire or shot-gun like clusters, we can also have accuracy/spread

invites.bloomPer.what: degrees more inaccuracy each volley while she keeps firing (the bloom); 0, none, and a bag adds its own.

invites.bloomDecay.what: degrees a second the bloom falls back by.

invites.bloomMax.what: the most degrees the bloom can reach.

invites.pierce.what: how many more creatures a 💌 flies on through after the first it lands on, each a hit as any letter's; 0, it stops at the first, and a bag adds its own (config/wardrobe.json invitesAdd).

decisions.quote: pierce, yes

invites.chain.what: how many hops a spent 💌 makes on to the nearest other invitable creature within chainRange metres (never one it has landed on, nor a stunned one), each a hit as any letter's; 0, none, and a bag adds its own (config/wardrobe.json invitesAdd).

decisions.quote: chain

invites.chainRange.what: how far (m) a chained 💌 looks for the next creature to hop to.

invites.linger.what: a 💌 that met no one rests where it came down this many seconds, fading over the last lingerFade, at most lingerMax at once (drawn only: it's no hit).

decisions.quote: invitations should sit on the ground for a little while before they fade away

invites.spin.what: How fast a 💌 spins in flight.

decisions.quote: the envelopes should spin like a frisbee

invites.spin.notes: a 💌 in flight lies flat and turns about the upright this many times a second (drawn only); when it lands it stops and lies flat.

invites.impact.what: how a 💌 landing on a creature feels (drawn only): a white flash for flash seconds, a squash of squash springing back over squashSecs, its ring slot popping in by pop over popSecs, and hitstop seconds of held picture on the 💌 that fills the ring.

decisions.quote: invitation impacts feel unsatisfying
decisions.rest: full hit feedback for a 💌 landing on a creature: a white flash, a little squash, its ring slot popping in, a thunk rising as the ring fills, a hitstop on the 💌 that fills it; no flash and a gentler squash with reduce-flashing on

invites.impact.notes: With reduce-flashing on there's no flash and the squash is gentle instead. The hitstop holds the picture only (the last frame kept, starting from the frame that shows the flash); the rules run on.

invites.cheer.what: one won over by her 💌s celebrates secs seconds by its body (render/cheer.ts), out of every fight meanwhile, a burst of that many hearts (hearts) off it.

decisions.quote: when a creature is won over ... it celebrates for about 1 s in a way that suits its body type
decisions.rest: hoppers a jump-spin, four-legged a roll-over, flyers a loop, the rest a wiggle-dance; hearts burst, the happy sting, its sigil flipping to the friends' colour with a pop; out of every fight meanwhile (a short rules hold)

invites.orbit.what: the 💌 ring circles a creature at scale times its body radius (movement.json bodies) plus gap metres, at least min, and at least height times its drawn height (to its top as drawn) plus gap, so it rings the creature you see at any size; wider still when it holds many.

decisions.quote: the orbits are smaller than the size of the creatures; their size should adjust depending on how large the creatures are
Invitation orbits are too tight around the creature
damage orbits are too wide, bring them in by around 30%
decisions.rest: scale 2 to 1.4, gap 1 to 0.7, min 2 to 1.4, height 0.9 to 0.63 (all x0.7); the soundsystem's 💥 ring 1.5 to 1.05 m outside it

invites.orbit.notes: A soundsystem's 💥 ring sits 1.5 gaps outside its radius.

invites.hard.what: the hard homing of the 💌s her Sentry and Slingshot hats throw: homing degrees a second, cone degrees either side it looks in, range metres it looks out to (was the legend buffs' charm, 420, 80 and 18).

invite.what: The old proximity chat, now replaced by the 💌 invite: she talked with the nearest creature in emoji.

decisions.rest: DESIGN.md, the leash; superseded by the 💌s, invites, and used only with invites.on false
losing a hit point is the cost

invite.notes: The old proximity chat [1]: on the ground, she talks by herself (no button: Ed, v244) to the nearest invitable creature within talkRange metres, and sticks with it; you chat in emoji for talkTime seconds (babies, young, adults), taking turns every turn seconds (babies, young, adults), then it is invited and leashed to you. Rising or moving further than cancelDistance stops it, and the chat's progress drains at decayRate of the rate it filled (0.5: half), so coming back soon picks up where it left off. Legends can't be invited: they give one unimpressed look. A legend gives her one unimpressed look for snubTime seconds per approach (not again till she's been beyond cancelDistance). Being hit doesn't set a chat back [2]. talkTime's fourth value is for legends let go on a knockout (wild legends still can't be invited).

win.what: The end of the route: after the last wave a pointer leads her to the remaining enraged creatures, then the victory lap.

decisions.quote: The end of the route
decisions.rest: rules/win.ts, docs/backlog/journey.md
a ring inside the conga's hid it from the ground

decisions.quote: Remove the end cards
decisions.rest: rules/guidance.ts; no card since Ed's

decisions.quote: when you're on the ground in the home area, the line should follow you

win.notes: The end of the route [1][2]: the last wave landed, a pointer to the enraged animal nearest the centre while any lives (enraged legends don't count; retarget: seconds between re-picks); none left, the victory lap: the pulse races back along the route to home at lapSpeed m/s, every stone it passes firing its fireworks; home reached, the night won: the dealt legends wake (bar any still enraged, which go back to sleep, their islands not found) and dance in place on its far side [3], north of the dancefloor beyond the conga, behind everything from the north-facing camera: on arcs legendGap m outside the conga's circle, legendRow m apart, legendSpace m between them, from due north out to legendArc degrees across, clear of the treehouse, the island's sigil flares on the dancefloor (drawn on over flareDraw s, held flare s), every other animal joins one conga line round it (congaSpeed m/s, congaGap m apart, a circle of at least congaRadius m, as big as the line needs), walking to its place at joinSpeed m/s (out of her sight, seen m off, simply there); once she reaches the party after the win (anywhere on the dancefloor, on foot or flying low: Ed, 2026-10-28), it settles: the guidance pins lead her home [4]. The conga follows her [5]: with follow on, while she's on the ground in the home area (not at the treehouse or in the treetops) the leader trails followLead m behind her along where she's walked and the rest follow single file congaGap apart, walking to their places at joinSpeed or followSpeed times her own speed, whichever is faster; anywhere else the line goes back round the dancefloor.

colourGrammar.what: The colour grammar: new, the party warm and the forest cold (her sigils pink, crimson, orange, gold by rank; the wild's purple, blue, turquoise; every baby pink, a sleeping legend lilac; berries pink; the ley line cold ahead of its spark); old, the colours before it.

quote: the forest is cold, the party is warm
red telegraphs are right; red does mean warning
should be less colourful; a cold coloured rainbow, maybe just blue and purple and turquoise
decisions.rest: his table: yours baby pink, youth red, adult orange, legend gold; wild youth purple, adult blue, legend turquoise; the last quote the ley line ahead of the pulse. The warnings keep their pure red; a youth's red is a crimson, toward rose and darker. The pause page's Colours switch (old: the friends' purple then three blues, the wild's purple then three reds, cherry-red berries, the whole rainbow ahead of the spark); it reloads the night

leash.length.what: how far a leashed creature roams from its leash point (you, or its sigil on the ground).

leash.runSpeed.what: how fast it hurries back when out of range (m/s).
leash.runSpeed.notes: how fast one out of range hurries back (m/s).

leash.pickRadius.what: how near a placed sigil you must be to pick it up.
leash.pickRadius.notes: how near (m) she picks up one of her own placed sigils.

leash.spacing.what: how close two sigils may be put down (keep it above pickRadius, or a blocked spot picks up instead of fizzling).
leash.spacing.notes: how far apart (m) sigils can be put down.

leash.runeRadius.what: how near (m) she picks up a happy creature's rune, a relic's sigil or her hat [1][2].

decisions.rest: both 25% further on: 3.5 to 4.375, 4.5 to 5.625

decisions.quote: Floor sigils of happy creatures and relics are difficult to pick up
decisions.rest: bigger than pickRadius, which stays under spacing, and less than a relic's sigilOffset, so standing on the relic itself doesn't

leash.hatHold.what: seconds she holds the sigil button on the ground, with nothing it picks up or puts down, to put her hat down at her feet (just a marker; a press over it puts it back on; rules/hat.ts putHat).

decisions.quote: If you are in ground mode and hold down the drop / pick up sigil button and there are no sigils to pick up, you put down your hat

leash.placedThrough.what: how bright a placed sigil shows where grass, bushes, trees or other scenery hide it (0 hidden, 1 as bright as in the open); never through the witch.

leash.sigilGlyph.what: How bright sigil glyphs are drawn, so they don't bloom into blobs on lit ground.

decisions.quote: it's their glow that makes them hard to see, not the pixellation

leash.sigilGlyph.notes: every sigil glyph from the leash atlas (placed, happy runes, the ghost, a relic's, her stack, the treetop projection, one walking home after a knockout) is drawn at sigilGlyph times its colour (0.5: under the bloom's threshold, so it doesn't bloom into a disc on lit ground; 1 as bright as before), and the soft halos under placed sigils, ready runes and relic sigils and round a relic in her stack at sigilHalo times their old strength (0: none).

leash.sigilBacking.what: A dark patch under every sigil on the ground, so it reads clearly.

quote: a dark patch directly underneath a sigil is quite helpful for making it more readable
the same width as the sigil, darker, edges not too smooth
sigils less transparent
decisions.rest: Bravo's o3

leash.sigilBacking.notes: under every sigil lying on the ground (placed, a happy creature's rune, the ghost, a relic's) a near-black disc in chunky 2-px cells with a lighter outer step, as wide as the glyph's own pixels times size, at dark (0: none), then the glyph painted opaque in its full neon at ink times how much it shows, under the dim added glyph (sigilGlyph).

leash.runeGap.what: a happy creature's rune lies south of it (down the screen), and a parked animal roams round a point the same way north of its sigil, by its size: its body radius, half the sigil with its backing, and runeGap metres between (rules/runeOffset.ts; it was a fixed restAbove, 5 m).

decisions.quote: Leashed animals should come to rest 10m above their placed sigil
decisions.rest: so it's easier to see and pick up

decisions.quote: the top of the sigil's background should be just below the animal's feet

leash.hex.what: Sigils are put down and picked up on a fixed hex grid on the ground, so a cluster of them reads cleanly.

decisions.quote: a cluster of placed sigils reads cleanly

leash.hex.notes: on the ground the sigil button works on a world-fixed hex grid, size metres between neighbouring cells (6 with the rank sigils, their ranks.hex; 4 before them, leash.spacing's density, as ?sigils=old still has it; 0: put down freely where she stands, as before). The cell nearest her decides: a sigil of hers in it, the press picks it up; free, a sigil goes down in its middle (never fizzling). Cells under a runestone or soundsystem (within stone metres of it, plus half a cell) or a home speaker (speaker metres) are skipped: the sigil goes down on the nearest free cell that isn't, within two cells, or not at all. Relic sigils and her hat go down where she stands, off the grid.

leash.runs.what: Holding the sigil button picks up, or puts down, sigils one after another as she runs.

decisions.quote: Pick up and place in runs

leash.runs.notes: with the sigil button held on since a press that picked a sigil up, she keeps picking up any sigil she runs over (her placed ones, happy creatures' runes, a relic's); held since a press that put one down, moving into each empty hex puts down the next (a press that did nothing starts no run, so holding E with nothing to do still puts her hat down). On the pad her hat is triangle's (placed or picked up), circle cycles the stack, L3 casts the broom's spell.

leash.runAfter.what: seconds the sigil button must be held since the press before a run starts, so a tap puts down or picks up exactly one sigil [1].

decisions.quote: It can be easy to put down or pick up more than one sigil when you tap the button, can we do something to make holds feel more deliberate?
decisions.rest: before, a run started on the press itself: a tap of about 0.1 s while walking (about 19 m/s) crossed into the next 6 m hex and put a second sigil down, or took a second sigil lying within reach. 0 is that old behaviour (?sigilfeel=old).

leash.sigilFeel.what: how a sigil travels between the ground and her stack, with a flash in its colour at each end, burning into the ground or sparkling round her stack [1][2].
leash.sigilFeel.notes: on: the transition (off: the snap and the amber ring as before, ?sigilfeel=old). fly: seconds it takes, eased in and out. arc: metres its path lifts in the middle. trail: sparkles trailing it. flash: the flashes' brightness. burn: seconds a put-down sigil glows as it burns in, settling to its resting look. sparkles: how many sparkle round her stack as one arrives. Only the drawing: the rules put it down or pick it up at once.

decisions.quote: Also make the floor<=>head transition more 'magical'.
have a distinct flash with each transition in the sigil colour, and it burns into the ground with a glow and sparkles above the head
decisions.rest: off (?sigilfeel=old): the sigil snaps into the stack and is written on the ground with the amber ring, as before. Only the drawing changes: the rules put the sigil down or pick it up at the same moment either way.

leash.runePull.what: on the ground, the nearest happy creature with its rune within radius (m) trots toward her at speed (m/s), stopping stop (m) from her, so its rune comes to her.

leash.chain.what: Every creature on her leash is on a chain this long; taut and moving away, she drags it, slowed by the heaviest taut chain's drag by level (a legend's stops her).

quote: adults are slow and heavy; you should be able to move within a reasonable distance from them (the size of a typical fight), but when the chain gets to its max length you can't move further until they move.
fine to start with
decisions.rest: 30 m to start, an anchor round each adult (replaced the same day by the 80 m chains, below); she can't take off while an adult is leashed (docs/plans/follower-buffs-and-challenge-areas.md)

quote: I don't think adults should be much faster; adult speed is a key balance factor. Instead, I agree that we should make chains longer and fixed length. Dragging youths slows you down a bit (e.g. 30%). Dragging adults slows you down a lot (e.g. 70%). Dragging legends slows you down completely (100%). Chains lie on the floor at full length so you can see how taut they are (though this might get messy-looking with many animals in a small space). Maybe they should all be the same length, about the size of a fight (80m?), so it mostly affects you when moving, not when fighting.
They don't stack, you are just affected by the heaviest one.
When you try and take off but you're weighed down by creatures, the chains rattle.
I think leashed youths shouldn't stop you from taking off, only adults and legends do.
A youth chain can make you rise more slowly, but effectively it's just a visual effect.
decisions.rest: replaces the 30 m adult anchor; a chain fades in by how far along it the creature is (invisible close, opaque and glowing taut)

leash.chain.notes: Only adults and legends stop her taking off. length (m, 80): every creature in her stack but babies (no chain) and a party legend (its own pin, legends.partyReach); a sleeping legend's sigil she carries tethers her at least this far (rules/sigilButton.ts). drag (youth 0.3, adult 0.7, legend 1): the share of her motion away a taut chain takes off; several taut: the heaviest; the creature is pulled after her at that pace, never faster than its top speed; her motion round it kept, never pulled in. She can't take off with an adult or legend on her leash; youths never stop her (rules/leashWeight.ts groundedBy). 0 length: no chains. Drawn: fadeFrom (0.3), the share of its length from which a chain shows, a smoothstep to whole at full length; glow (0.6), how much brighter it is taut; rattle: a refused take-off's jolt down the weighing chains, strength m at her end, for time s (and its sound, sfx.rattle). youthRise (0.85): with a youth on her leash her rise is drawn this much slower (drawn only: when she counts as up for the rules is unchanged).

leash.chain.taut.what: Pulling on a taut chain: up in the treetops it drags her down to the ground, on foot it slides that sigil out of her stack and puts it down, and a legend's chain yanks her back instead; with a lighter drag on foot and the chains' look.

decisions.quote: When you are in treetop mode and you are pulling a creature on its chain, when the chain gets taut you should be pulled back to ground mode. This shouldn't be a sudden transition, but as you pull outside of the length you are progressively pulled down; if you stop pulling, you rise up again, only if you keep pulling do you actually fully switch back to ground mode.
decisions.rest: before: nothing pulled her out of the sky (Ed, 2026-11-03)

decisions.quote: the transition from treetop to ground isn't smooth; she is pulled down some of the way, and then falls to the ground.
decisions.rest: his playtest of v7948; so the pull carries her all the way down in one curve and she is in ground mode as she arrives: the tug's commit knob went, its hold and ease came, its perMetre 0.022 to 0.05 to keep it about 3 s

quote: Treetop pulldown is somewhat gradual - you have to tug for a while before you're pulled down. pop-out should also be gradual - you pull against a chain, the chain goes taut and you can see the sigil in your stack being pulled out, and only if you keep pulling it plops onto the ground as if placed. So the whole treetop-ground-pop is several seconds and neither part can be accidental. Also pulling on the ground should slow you down less than pulling in the air ... so it should feel possible to 'pull your creatures on the ground' without accidentally dropping them everywhere.
legend chains yank you back instead of popping out
adult chains should look larger, and legend chains should look larger still.
decisions.rest: through the coordinator: ground drag about youth 0.15, adult 0.4; a taut creature about 1.5 times its leash pace; about 2 to 3 s of steady pulling pops; one sigil at a time; chain sizes youth 1, adult about 1.6, legend about 2.4

decisions.quote: chains are currently the colour of the sigil; instead I'd like them to be more generally 'magic chain' coloured, with the sigil colour as a occasional flash along it. Chains are a bit too visually dominant at the moment.
decisions.rest: he chose one shared pale, cool silvery violet, slightly see-through; the flash runs from the creature to her stack, staggered per chain. Big youth armies: tuning only (the drag knobs), no count-based stacking

leash.chain.taut.notes: on (true); off (?tautchain=0) every part below off, the chains as before. groundDrag (youth 0.15, adult 0.4, legend 1): on foot, the share of her motion away a taut chain takes off (in the air leash.chain.drag), and the creature is pulled along at her pace less it, not held to its own top speed (leash.runSpeed's 4 m/s for most, which held her to about that). hurry (1.5): a creature whose chain is taut runs after her this many times its leash pace (its own steps: rules/leash.ts stepLeashed, rules/travel.ts). tug: up in the treetops, perMetre (0.05; 0.022 till 2026-11-13) of the way from the treetops to the ground (her lift held at 1 - that, so her height, her speed's blend, the canopy and the camera all follow the one eased curve an ordinary descent draws, only slower) each metre her step pulls past the tautest chain's end (counted from rules/tautChain.ts PULL_FROM 2 m/s, below which she's coasting round the end, to PULL_MOST 16 m/s); her pull's pace eased over ease (0.15) s, so it comes on gently and one step's hitch in the chain doesn't show (0: not eased); rise (0.3) of the way back up a second not pulling, from however low; pulled all the way she is at the ground and in ground mode there, with no drop (till 2026-11-13 the pull stopped commit, 0.4, of the way down and the ordinary descent dropped her the rest: about 14 m in a third of a second); hold (0.4): over a lake's water or a treehouse floor, where she can't come down, the furthest of the way down the pull takes her (lower already, she eases back up to it at rise). Dragging a youth that's about 2.8 s of sustained pull, at most about 17 m/s of descent in the middle. pop: on foot, pulling a youth's or an adult's chain (going on past its end faster than it follows, PULL_FROM 2 m/s or more) fills a meter for the one pulled hardest (one at a time; it keeps the one it has while that's still pulled), full after fill (2.5) s of steady pulling; easing off drains it in drain (1.5) s; full, that sigil is put down where she stands by the ordinary put-down. yank: pulling past a legend's chain she's thrown back toward it metres (4) m by the knock's easing throw, with no stagger, at most once every every (1.2) s, and its chain rattles; a legend's sigil never pops; the sleeping legend's tether stays a hard hold. links (0.62, 1, 1.5 m): the chains' link size by rank, youth, adult, legend (leash.ranks.chain.link's 0.62, 0.78, 1 when off; the tether keeps its own). look: every chain colour (184, 182, 210) at alpha (0.6), its taut glow times glow (0.35) of leash.chain.glow, its link glows dimmer; flash: its sigil's colour runs from the creature to her stack for time (0.9) s every every (4) s, staggered by chain, width (0.14) of its length either side; a sigil being pulled out flashes up to four times as often. Her broom's pull (the Canoe hull) scales a youth's and an adult's drag, the tug and the pop.

decisions.rest: each baby keeps half the one in front's length, half its own and margin between their middles, never under gap

leash.babies.notes: her leashed babies following her on the ground walk in single file along where she's been, in stack order (the stack's bottom one first), each clear of the one in front by their sizes [4]: half the one in front's length, half its own and margin (1) metres between their middles, never under gap (5) metres; half a baby's length is its drawn body (rules/combatSpacing.ts drawnRadius, the calibrated drawing at its kind and level) times size (0.75: that disc's corner overstates the side-on sprite), and the first keeps the same off her, her own half her (1.75) metres (her side-on sprite is about 3.5 m long). A baby fox or squirrel stays gap apart; a baby bear about 8 m, an elephant or rhino about 10, a crocodile about 20 (rules/babies.ts queueGap); while she's in a fight they scatter, scatter metres or a quarter more off to the side away from the first attacker [2] (and half its length further, so a big one is out of view end to end), for the whole fight [3]: from the moment something goes for her or one of hers (closing in or winding up, not on the hit), the same way throughout, back into line once nothing has for calm seconds; one more than farAt metres from her (about off the screen) moves at farSpeed m/s, so it's with her in seconds.

leash.ranks.notes: on [2], every leash sigil (her stack, placed sigils, happy runes, the ghost, the treetop projection, the bond) is its bare glyph, no ring or disc, glyph metres across on the ground, in its rank's colour (colours: baby, youth, adult, legend; the species' neon stays the world's: borders, stones, fireworks, dancefloor, holograms, chart), with embers rising off its strokes (embers.count at once, each size metres, rising rise metres, by rank; in her stack stack of that), under a dark shade in the glyph's own shape (not a disc); a baby or a youth in her stack shows two rows of round dots off to its right, one a berry it needs to grow (toEvolve, every one fed by her since 2026-11-03; before, the last was eaten only at a placed sigil), at most dotsPerRow a row, bright eaten and dim not, pulsing when ready, the next twinkling while a berry is queued for it; and the hex grid is hex metres (leash.hex.size).

bond.what: How a leashed creature shows its tie to its sigil: a glow at its feet, sparks, and a thread when the leash is strained.

decisions.quote: The curve on slack leashes should be higher than it is now
The arc of leashes should be higher
decisions.rest: doubled, 0.4 to 0.8 and the cap 4 to 8

bond.notes: how a creature shows its tie to its sigil (rim: a glow at its feet in the sigil's colour; sparks: one spark every sparkEvery seconds from sigil to creature, staggered; thread: a dotted line only under strain). The bond between her and her leashed creatures: rim, a glow at a creature's feet in its sigil's colour; sparks, one now and then from sigil to creature (every sparkEvery seconds, staggered); thread, a dotted line while a leash is under strain (past 0.85 of its length), bowing upward by threadArcSlack metres per metre of its length while slack, flattening to threadArcTaut as it goes taut [1][2], never more than threadArcMax metres.

When you have multiple ones of the same species, the inactive buff icons are blue. When a buff is inactive, it twinkles in pink.
decisions.rest: every leashed adult and legend shows its icon(s): amber active, blue redundant (#2d6eff, the wild adult's), pink twinkling unfed (#c8228c, the berries')

buffs.notes: groups: each group's retreats (a kind's art/creatures/<id>/creature.js retreat decides its group). legend: the stacks a leashed legend gives (no berries needed). pips: max an adult holds, life seconds each (draining one at a time while it follows her; parked ones keep theirs), warn seconds before one fades it twinkles in her stack, start pips a new adult has before it has eaten (1). Per stack: climbers.dash more dash charges; darters.speed her speed times 1 + it; stalkers.speed and stalkers.range her 💌s' speed and range times 1 + each; heavies.shots more ways her shots go round her, clockwise, her fire rate times the ways (1 stack: a second shot opposite between each, 2: three at 120° at 3×); packHunters.rate her fire rate times 1 + it and packHunters.spread degrees more inaccuracy; shells.chain more chain hops, on top of the bag's. icons: blue, a redundant icon's colour (another of its kind gives the buff); pink, an unfed adult's, twinkling once a twinkle s.
